title: Summarization is Not Dead Yet
abstract: arXiv:2606.08000v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: The progress of large language models (LLMs) has fueled claims that model-generated summaries rival or even surpass human-written references, raising questions about whether summarization remains an open research problem. We re-examine this narrative through a multi-track evaluation covering diverse datasets and state-of-the-art LLMs, combining controlled human assessment, bias-mitigated LLM-as-Judge protocols, factuality verification against external knowledge, and corpus-level linguistic analysis. Our findings reveal a more nuanced landscape in which human references continue to demonstrate advantages in informativeness and faithfulness, whereas LLM outputs are preferred mainly for surface-level coherence and fluency. translated_abstract: arXiv:2606.08000v2 公告类型：替换-交叉 摘要：大型语言模型（LLMs）的进展引发了声称模型生成的摘要可与人类撰写的参考文献相媲美甚至超越其质量的言论，这引发了对摘要生成是否仍是一个开放研究问题的质疑。我们通过一项多轨评估重新审视了这一叙事，该评估涵盖了多样化的数据集和最先进的LLMs，结合了受控人类评估、缓解偏差的LLM作为评审者协议、针对外部知识的事实核查，以及语料库层面的语言分析。我们的发现揭示了一个更为细致的图景：人类参考文献在信息性和忠实性方面继续展现优势，而LLM输出主要在表面连贯性和流畅性方面被偏好。事实核查表明，人类参考文献仍更为可靠，尤其是涉及推理或综合的声明，而语言分析则揭示了跨模型输出的风格同质化模式。
tldr: 摘要生成并未消亡，人类参考文献在信息性和忠实性上仍优于LLM输出，后者仅胜在表面流畅性。
en_tdlr: Summarization is not dead; human references still outperform LLM outputs in informativeness and faithfulness, while LLMs only excel in surface-level fluency.
